svg.text: SPOTIFY — PLAYBACK STATE & THE next() DECISION
TRANSPORT STATE — lives on PlaybackSession
STOPPED
initial state · position = 0
stop() does NOT clear the queue
PLAYING
the only state advanceTime() acts on
currentSong != null, position ticking
PAUSED
position PRESERVED
the clock stops advancing
play(song)
position ← 0, playCount++
pause()
resume()
stop()
also: next() at end of queue
stop()
next / previous / seek
Both transitions are GUARDED, so the machine cannot be walked backwards:
pause() checks state == PLAYING · resume() checks state == PAUSED && currentSong != null
Double-pause, resume-from-stopped, pause-with-nothing-loaded: all silent no-ops.
There is no BUFFERING / LOADING / ERROR state — nothing here touches a network.
A real client needs at least BUFFERING, and the pause guard would then have to
accept it too — say that before the interviewer says it.
Note play() ALWAYS restarts at position 0 and always bumps Song.playCount, so
a repeat-ONE track re-counts every loop. Whether that is right is a product call.
queue.next() — four branches, in this exact order
1. queue.isEmpty() → return null → session.stop()
2. repeatMode == ONE → return the SAME song, index unchanged
checked BEFORE the bounds test, so repeat-ONE pins you even mid-queue
3. currentIndex < size − 1 → ++currentIndex, return that song
the ordinary case — one step forward through the list
4. at the end + repeatMode == ALL → currentIndex = 0, wrap around
this is the ONLY branch that can loop forever
otherwise → return null → PlaybackSession.next() calls stop()
"null means the queue is exhausted" — the session, not the queue, decides to stop
previous() is deliberately NOT symmetric:
index > 0 ⇒ step back · at index 0 with ALL ⇒ wrap to the last track ·
at index 0 with NONE ⇒ returns the CURRENT song, so the session replays it.
Note previous() ignores repeatMode == ONE entirely — with repeat-ONE on, next()
pins the track but previous() still walks backwards. Asymmetric, arguably a bug.
hasNext() answers true forever under ONE or ALL — that is what auto-advance reads.
setShuffle — what it really does
setShuffle(true):
1. no-op if already on (idempotent) ✓
2. originalOrder ← copy of the queue
3. Fisher-Yates over the WHOLE list
4. swap the playing song to index 0
5. currentIndex = 0
before — playing track 3 of 6

svg.text: The current track keeps playing — that part is right ✓
But it shuffles the ENTIRE queue, including already-played
tracks, and pins the index to 0 — so your listening history is
gone. previous() can no longer reach A or B. Real players
shuffle only the REMAINING tail and keep the played prefix.
Turning shuffle OFF restores originalOrder verbatim — so any
song added while shuffled DISAPPEARS from the queue.
Random is unseeded ⇒ a shuffle test cannot assert an order.

g.text: AUTO-ADVANCE: WHERE THE TWO MACHINES MEET
advanceTime(seconds) is the only place transport state and queue navigation
touch. It runs only when state == PLAYING, adds to currentPositionSeconds,
and at end-of-track asks queue.hasNext():
true → next() → play(nextSong) — stays PLAYING, position resets
false → stop() — STOPPED, position 0, queue untouched
The clock is a PARAMETER, not a thread. That single choice is why every
playback scenario in the demo is deterministic and needs no sleeps.
THE ORDER OF THE BRANCHES IS THE DESIGN
Swap branch 2 and branch 3 and repeat-ONE stops working: you
would advance normally and only pin the track at the very end
of the queue. Repeat-ONE has to win before the bounds check.
Same for branch 4: wrap-around is only reachable AFTER the
"is there a next index" test fails.
When an interviewer asks "what if repeat and shuffle are both
on?" — they are orthogonal: shuffle reorders, repeat re-enters.
THE THREE FIXES WORTH VOLUNTEERING
1. Shuffle the TAIL only: keep queue[0..currentIndex] fixed, Fisher-Yates the
rest. History survives, previous() still works, no index pinning.
2. Rebuild originalOrder on every add, or store a shuffle PERMUTATION instead
of a snapshot — then un-shuffling cannot lose songs.
3. Stop clear() from resetting shuffle/repeat. They are USER PREFERENCES
that outlive a queue; today playSong() silently wipes both.
Inject the Random for reproducibility while you are in there.

svg.text: WHITEBOARD ORDER:

① the three transport states and the two guarded transitions → ② queue.next() as an ordered branch ladder (ONE beats bounds beats ALL) → ③ draw the shuffle strip before/after → then advanceTime as the join
LEGEND
